questions.question: In what application is gallium arsenide used as a semiconductor material?
Which of the following semiconductor materials contains excess free electrons?
Why does a PN-junction diode not conduct current when reverse biased?

choices.A: Only P-type semiconductor material can conduct current
choices.B: Only N-type semiconductor material can conduct current
choices.C: Holes in P-type material and electrons in the N-type material are separated by the applied voltage, widening the depletion region
choices.D: Excess holes in P-type material combine with the electrons in N-type material, converting the entire diode into an insulator

questions.answer: Holes in P-type material and electrons in the N-type material are separated by the applied voltage, widening the depletion region

questions.question: What is the name given to an impurity atom that adds holes to a semiconductor crystal structure?
How does DC input impedance at the gate of a field-effect transistor (FET) compare with that of a bipolar transistor?

choices.B: An FET has lower input impedance
choices.C: An FET has higher input impedance

questions.answer: An FET has higher input impedance

questions.question: What is the beta of a bipolar junction transistor?

choices.A: The frequency at which the current gain is reduced to 0.707
choices.B: The change in collector current with respect to the change in base current
choices.C: The breakdown voltage of the base-to-collector junction

questions.answer: The change in collector current with respect to the change in base current

questions.question: Which of the following indicates that a silicon NPN junction transistor is biased on?

choices.A: Base-to-emitter resistance of approximately 6 ohms to 7 ohms
choices.B: Base-to-emitter resistance of approximately 0.6 ohms to 0.7 ohms
choices.C: Base-to-emitter voltage of approximately 6 volts to 7 volts
choices.D: Base-to-emitter voltage of approximately 0.6 volts to 0.7 volts

questions.answer: Base-to-emitter voltage of approximately 0.6 volts to 0.7 volts

questions.question: What is the term for the frequency at which the grounded-base current gain of a bipolar junction transistor has decreased to 0.7 of the gain obtainable at 1 kHz?
What is a depletion-mode field-effect transistor (FET)?

choices.A: An FET that exhibits a current flow between source and drain when no gate voltage is applied
choices.B: An FET that has no current flow between source and drain when no gate voltage is applied
choices.C: An FET that exhibits very high electron mobility due to a lack of holes in the N-type material
choices.D: An FET for which holes are the majority carriers

questions.answer: An FET that exhibits a current flow between source and drain when no gate voltage is applied

What is the purpose of connecting Zener diodes between a MOSFET gate and its source or drain?

choices.A: To provide a voltage reference for the correct amount of reverse-bias gate voltage
choices.B: To protect the substrate from excessive voltages
choices.C: To keep the gate voltage within specifications and prevent the device from overheating
choices.D: To protect the gate from static damage

questions.answer: To protect the gate from static damage

questions.question: What is the most useful characteristic of a Zener diode?

choices.A: A constant current drop under conditions of varying voltage
choices.B: A constant voltage drop under conditions of varying current
choices.D: An internal capacitance that varies with the applied voltage

questions.answer: A constant voltage drop under conditions of varying current

choices.A: In oscillator circuits as the negative resistance element
